links.note: Greek “with a fist” is rendered as washing the forearms.
The middle verb expresses washing themselves.
Greek says “unclean”; English specifies unwashed hands.
The dative of “lips” expresses the means of honoring.
Greek “die by death” is rendered “be put to death.”
English supplies the recipient of the gift.
The participle means making clean; its subject is left implicit in English.
English adds “For”; SBL instead has “but, immediately.”
English combines the relative pronoun and repeated possessive as “whose.”
English names Jesus, the subject implicit in “said.”
Greek says they eat “from” the crumbs; English leaves “from” implicit.
The adjective means having difficulty speaking.
The middle participle describes taking someone aside.
This timing word has no SBL counterpart.
